decks.label: Whose Eyes? topics
decks.description: Topics with many stakeholders, every one supports 20+ different viewpoints.

prompts.text: our school's homework policy
the school cafeteria and what it serves
a new skate park being built where the empty lot is
the town deciding whether to cut down a 200-year-old oak to widen the road
a family deciding whether to move to a new city for a job
the invention of the automobile
the Louisiana Purchase
a dam being built on a river
the first day a new student joins our class
a viral video filmed in a public place
the class pet nobody remembered to feed over break
artificial intelligence writing students' essays

decks.label: Both Sides of the Rope claims
decks.description: Claims with real evidence on both sides, none of them settled, all of them school-safe.

prompts.text: Homework should be optional.
Every student should learn to code.
School should start two hours later.
Zoos do more good than harm.
Books are better than their movie versions.
It's better to be a specialist than a generalist.
Group projects should be graded as a group, one grade for everyone.
Humanity should send people to Mars this century.
The school year should be spread across the whole year with more breaks.
Learning an instrument should be required in school.
Athletes deserve their salaries.
A rebuilt ship with every plank replaced is still the same ship.

decks.label: Social studies claims
decks.description: Civics and history claims with honest evidence on both sides.

prompts.text: The federal government should have more power during a crisis.
Geography shapes a country's history more than its leaders do.
The Industrial Revolution did more good than harm.
Voting should be required by law.
Trade between countries makes war less likely.
A primary source is more trustworthy than a textbook.
Cities should replace old statues that honor people we no longer admire.
The best way to change an unfair law is to work inside the system.

decks.label: Social studies perspective topics
decks.description: Historical moments and civic decisions with many stakeholders.

prompts.text: the signing of the Declaration of Independence
the California Gold Rush
the building of the transcontinental railroad
women winning the right to vote
a town deciding whether to remove an old statue from the square
the invention of the printing press
a new factory opening in a small farming town
the first year of a brand-new country writing its constitution

decks.label: English and ELA claims
decks.description: Claims about stories, authors, and reading that split a room.

prompts.text: A story's villain matters more than its hero.
Reading fiction teaches you more about people than studying facts.
Some books should be required reading for everyone.
Poetry can say things plain language cannot.
An author's life should change how we read their books.
Happy endings are overrated.

decks.label: English and ELA perspective topics
decks.description: Story moments and book-world dilemmas worth seeing through other eyes.

prompts.text: the moment the main character makes their biggest mistake
a banned book arriving at the school library
an author deciding how their story should end
a small town where the newspaper prints its last issue
the villain's version of the story

decks.label: Science claims
decks.description: Science and technology claims where the evidence genuinely pulls both ways.

prompts.text: Space exploration is worth the cost.
Humans should try to bring back extinct species.
Nuclear power is the best replacement for fossil fuels.
Scientists should be allowed to edit genes to prevent disease.
Robots should do every job that is dangerous for humans.
Every big scientific discovery eventually gets used for both good and harm.

decks.label: Science perspective topics
decks.description: Discoveries and dilemmas that look different to everyone they touch.

prompts.text: a new wind farm planned for the ridge above town
the discovery of antibiotics
a plan to reintroduce wolves to a national park
the first mission to settle Mars
a drought forcing a town to decide who gets water first

decks.label: Story Builder seeds
decks.description: Open-ended premises with somewhere to go, every one supports twenty different stories.

prompts.text: A mysterious door appears in the school hallway overnight.
The class pet has been keeping a secret.
At exactly noon, every screen in the world shows the same face.
The substitute teacher is definitely not from around here.
A message in a bottle washes up, dated fifty years in the future.
The elevator has only one button, and it is labeled MAYBE.
On the last day of summer, the ocean quietly disappears.
Somebody's homework starts answering back.
The town's statues switch places every night.
A tiny dragon is living in the school's lost and found.

decks.label: Someone's Got You openers
decks.description: Low-stakes versions of "what are you working on?", pick the one that fits the week.

prompts.text: One thing you're working on, wrestling with, or quietly proud of this week. Small is fine. 'trying to get more sleep' counts. One sentence.
Something coming up that you're a little nervous about, a test, a tryout, a conversation. One sentence.
One thing you did recently that took effort, even if nobody noticed. One sentence.
A goal you're chipping away at, school or not. One sentence.
Something you're trying to get better at right now. One sentence.
